milestones.title: My Academic Journey
milestones.subtitle: UNISA - Computer Science (Fisciano)
milestones.imageCaption: Me presenting my thesis project, explaining the work on comparing different Machine Learning algorithms for image classification.
milestones.content:
From 2018 to December 2022 I studied Computer Science at UNISA: **object-oriented programming in Java**, **distributed programming with Java EE**, **web development with HTML, CSS and JavaScript**, and **mathematics and statistics** applied with **Python**.

My thesis, *"Comparison of Machine Learning Algorithms for Image Classification"*, compared classification models on the **Fashion-MNIST** dataset.

I also built practical projects end to end, including an e-commerce platform for automotive products, front end and back end. Working in student teams, I learned to coordinate the work and to be someone the others could rely on.

milestones.title: Internship at SI2001
milestones.subtitle: Full-Stack Developer Intern
milestones.content:
Full-stack internship at **SI2001**, on web applications built with Spring Boot and Angular.

I built front-end components, integrated REST APIs, wrote back-end business logic and managed databases, on real projects inside a structured team. In March 2023 I joined SI2001 permanently.

milestones.title: Permanent Position at SI2001
milestones.subtitle: Full-Stack Developer
milestones.imageCaption: Me at my remote workstation, surrounded by screens and code.
milestones.content:
Today I work on the **back end** of the European core banking systems of **Intesa Sanpaolo**, with Java, Spring Boot, Spring Batch and PostgreSQL.

Before that, I worked on the **front end** of **more than five projects** with Vue.js, Angular and Flutter.

I work in Agile teams, taking part in sprint planning, daily stand-ups and retrospectives.

list.title: Sfrigola Core
list.content: **Sfrigola Core** is the REST API of Sfrigola, a digital recipe book I build as a personal exercise. Built with **Spring Boot**, it handles recipes, ingredients, categories and tags (multi-language and searchable), ratings, favourites and a draft-to-publish workflow with role-based access for users, contributors and admins.

list.title: Sfrigola App
list.content: **Sfrigola App** is the **Flutter** mobile app of Sfrigola, for iOS and Android: curated recipe feeds, search by category and favourites, on a feature-based architecture with a custom design system and type-safe routing. It consumes the Sfrigola Core API.

list.title: Comparing Machine Learning Algorithms for Image Classification
list.content:
**Artificial Intelligence** is spreading across many fields and offers a wide range of application contexts.

Image recognition and classification are among the areas that enable some of its most impressive results.

The purpose of this research is to analyze the most well-known classification algorithms, such as **K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN)**, **Decision Trees**, **Random Forest**, **Support Vector Machines (SVM)**, and **Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs)**.

The goal is to evaluate their efficiency in classifying the sample images contained in the **MNIST** and **Fashion-MNIST (F-MNIST)** datasets.

The study was carried out using **Python** libraries, particularly **Scikit-learn**.

These libraries provide implementations of the algorithms and allow fine-tuning of their parameters.

This makes it possible to identify which parameters most influence learning capability and to improve classification accuracy when the models are trained on the provided datasets.

The behavior of the algorithms helped clarify the reasons behind the transition from **MNIST**—now considered outdated and overused—to its successor, **Fashion-MNIST**.

With the same parameter settings, the examined algorithms show lower classification accuracy on **F-MNIST** compared to **MNIST**.

This highlights that **F-MNIST** is more challenging and therefore requires closer consideration of algorithm characteristics to achieve high accuracy.

Despite this increased difficulty, these algorithms still achieve strong performance when trained on **F-MNIST**.

This confirms their ability to generalize and provide efficient results on other existing datasets as well.

list.title: Studio Legale Romano
list.content:
After launching the site in 2025, I keep working with the firm: I'm redesigning the website and building new products for it.

- **PraticaSicura**, a portal for requesting flight refunds
- **Domus** (front-end) and **Cardo** (back-end), the internal system the firm uses to manage its cases

The firm commissioned the **Studio Legale Romano** website as a modern, professional showcase. I designed and built the whole interface: the firm's history and values, a full profile for each lawyer with their areas of practice, and a services section that helps visitors find the right area quickly.

Contact details are visible from every page, and the opening hours update in real time.

list.title: Guess My Number
list.content:
The game follows a level-based progression system: each match starts with **five lives**, and the objective is to guess a randomly generated number between **1 and 20** before running out of attempts.

Every game begins with five lives, and your goal is to find the correct number within that limit.

Every **five levels**, you unlock a **bonus stage** where you must identify the correct number from three possible choices.

**Try to beat your best score!**

list.title: Pig Game
list.content:
The game is a **1 vs 1 challenge** between two players, configured at the beginning of each new match.

The active player starts their turn by rolling a die. The value obtained can either be saved and added to their total score, or they can choose to roll again in an attempt to accumulate more points.

However, pushing your luck comes with a risk: if the die lands on **1**, the player loses all the points accumulated during that turn that have not yet been saved, and the turn immediately passes to the opponent.

The game ends when one of the two players is the first to reach **exactly 100 points**.

list.title: sb-floating-panel-vue
list.content:
**sb-floating-panel-vue** is a headless **Vue 3** library for floating panels (dropdowns, menus, listboxes, popovers and tooltips), built on **{'@'}floating-ui/vue**.

You write three components, **SbContainer**, **SbReference** and **SbFloating**; the library handles placement, flipping, viewport collisions, open state, keyboard and accessibility. It ships no CSS: your styles read its data attributes and CSS variables, so it fits plain CSS, Tailwind or CSS modules.

- **Accessible by default**: ARIA naming, the WAI-ARIA keyboard model of menus and listboxes, tooltips that meet WCAG 1.4.13, Tab order kept across the teleport, focus management, Escape and click outside
- **Reactive**: every prop, **v-model:open**, nested panels and submenus
- **Typed**: every prop, slot prop, event and option type is exported

It is published on npm, with CI and test coverage tracked on GitHub.
